prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In Frames 1–3, the depth map captures the upward-sloping geometry of the cliff face receding from bright foreground boulders (1–2 m away on the bottom-left and bottom-right) and the standing belayer in blue on the left (2–3 m away, facing the wall) to the climber ascending above them (8–12 m away, 4–6 m higher) and a distant person on the right ledge (10–15 m away). A person in a yellow helmet enters the bottom-right foreground within 1–1.5 m in Frames 1 and 3 (cropped out in Frame 2) facing the camera wearer, before the camera turns sharply downward in Frame 4 and slightly up in Frame 5. In Frames 4–5, bright near-field values show the camera wearer's own legs, shoes, and reaching right hand within 0.5–0.8 m (within arm's reach) at the bottom, flanked by boulders at 1–2 m and the seated red-shirted person on the left in Frame 5 at 1–1.5 m looking toward the camera wearer against a dark canyon backdrop (>50 m away). Compared to RGB, the depth map makes the continuous distance gradient across textured rock and the distinct depth separation between foreground boulders, the belayer, and the cliff face immediately apparent. However, it is unreliable on thin climbing ropes (which disappear completely), blends the high climber's upper body into the rock wall in Frames 2–3, and saturates to uniform white across the nearest limbs and foreground figures in Frames 1–3.
descriptions.segmentation: Across Frames 1–3, instance segmentation isolates the standing belayer on the bottom-left (2–3 m away, facing away, waist occluded by the bottom edge) and the climber 5–8 m behind and above them on the rock wall (8–12 m from the camera wearer, facing the cliff), plus the head and shoulders of a third person looking toward the camera wearer in the bottom-right of Frame 3 (1–1.5 m away). As the camera tilts down to the ground in Frame 4 and pans in Frame 5, the masks shift to the camera wearer's own lower legs and feet at the bottom center (0.5–0.8 m away, within arm's reach), the seated person on the left in Frame 5 (1–1.5 m away, facing and looking at the camera wearer with arms resting on their knees), and the camera wearer's right hand and forearm at the bottom-right edge (<0.5 m away). The map clarifies crisp person-versus-background boundaries where earth-toned clothing and skin blend with the sandstone in RGB, especially for the distant climber on the cliff face. However, it fails to segment any non-person objects such as boulders, helmets, ropes, or loose climbing shoes on the ground, completely misses the distant person on the right rock ledge in Frames 1–3 and the partially visible helmet in Frame 1, and fragments the camera wearer's left leg and shoe in Frame 4 into two overlapping 'person' instances.
descriptions.pose: In Frame 1, the pose map detects only a partial upper-body skeleton for the standing belayer on the bottom-left (2–3 m away, facing the cliff with their lower body out of view), while Frames 2–4 contain no skeleton detections at all as the camera shifts from the cliff face down to the ground. In Frame 5, a yellow body skeleton captures the seated person on the left (1–1.5 m from the camera wearer), showing their head cluster oriented toward the camera wearer, torso angled slightly right, and both arms bent with wrists resting near their knees and ankles (within their own arm's reach, roughly 0.5–1 m to the left of the central boulder). Where present, the skeleton makes the seated person's joint positions, folded-leg posture, and head orientation toward the camera wearer explicit without interference from shadows or clothing folds. However, the pose map is highly sparse and unreliable across the sequence, missing the belayer entirely in Frames 2–3, failing to detect the ascending climber (8–12 m away) and distant right-ledge figure (10–15 m away), missing the close-up head in Frame 3, and failing to render any body or magenta hand skeletons for the camera wearer's own limbs and hands within 0.5 m in Frames 4–5.
